claims.assertion: From the Q1 FY2027 10-Q onward, NVIDIA's risk factors add that it has assisted authorities regarding attempted diversion and that it lacks physical control of products after sale, relying on customers' and partners' compliance programs. The phrase 'physical control' is absent from the FY2026 10-K and Q3 FY2026 10-Q.
claims.pinpoint: 10-Q Q1 FY2027 Item 1A; 10-Q Q2 FY2027 Item 1A
claims.supporting_passage: "We have provided and will continue to provide assistance to authorities regarding attempted diversion, but as we do not have physical control of our products after sale, we must also rely on the compliance programs of our customers and partners."
excluded_implications: That diversion of NVIDIA products at scale occurred
That the change was a response to the short report
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The change could reflect the DOJ cases already public, routine legal review, or the short report; the filing does not say.

claims.assertion: China (incl. Hong Kong) HQ revenue was $4,550m in Q1 FY2027 and $7,880m in Q2 FY2027. NVIDIA states Hopper Data Center shipments to China in Q2 FY2027 were under 1% of Data Center revenue ($89.0bn), and that it shipped uncontrolled products such as gaming and workstation GPUs to China.
claims.pinpoint: 10-Q Q1 and Q2 FY2027, geographic note; MD&A; Item 1A
claims.supporting_passage: "Shipments of Data Center Hopper products to China during the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 were less than 1% of Data Center revenue."
excluded_implications: That China-linked demand outside China-HQ customers rose or fell
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Higher China-HQ revenue is consistent with uncontrolled-product sales; it neither confirms nor refutes indirect channels.

claims.assertion: The Singapore Police Force stated on 30 October 2026 that 'Investigations into Megaspeed are ongoing' and that Singapore does not implement foreign unilateral export controls but acts against fraud. In response to a newspaper report, it stated that 'there were no such investigations conducted in respect of' the individual named in that report; 'such' refers to investigations into alleged ties to the NVIDIA CEO or to PRC intelligence.
claims.pinpoint: SPF clarification statement, Government response paras 1–3 and statement para 3
claims.supporting_passage: "Investigations into Megaspeed are ongoing. We are unable to comment further at this juncture."
excluded_implications: Any finding of wrongdoing by Megaspeed or NVIDIA
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: An ongoing investigation is not an adverse finding.

claims.assertion: NVIDIA's board accepted the CEO's resignation on 11 November 2026 and appointed the CFO interim CEO; the 8-K and press release state no reason.
claims.supporting_passage: "the Board of Directors, or the Board, of NVIDIA Corporation accepted the resignation of Jen-Hsun Huang"
excluded_implications: Any link between the resignation and supply-chain or export-control matters
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Press reports attribute the resignation to personal conduct; the primary filing does not.

claims.assertion: From the 12 May 2026 close: NVDA +2.29% on 13 May and +4.39% on 14 May; market-model CAR[0,+1] = +4.6% vs SMH (t = 2.22) and +4.2% vs SPY (t = 1.84). CAR[0,+10] = −6.5% vs both (t ≈ −1.3). Buy-and-hold to 13 Nov 2026: NVDA −26.1%, SMH −13.3%, SPY +2.7%.
excluded_implications: That the report caused any of these moves
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Earnings on day +5 (SI1-PST-006), an acquisition (SI1-PST-005), the CEO resignation (SI1-PST-003) and sector moves sit inside the windows. No CAR exceeds the Bonferroni-adjusted threshold (|t| > 2.73 for 8 tests); see erratum SI1-PE-02.

claims.assertion: Per secondary summaries, the short report alleged that over 20% of FY2026 compute revenue remained China-driven via diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries, derived from third-party market-share estimates and per-unit price assumptions, and it relied on trade records, Singapore/Malaysia corporate filings and interviews.
claims.supporting_passage: Not quoted from the original (not retrieved)
claims.scope: Allegation by a disclosed short seller, 13 May 2026
excluded_implications: Any finding that the allegation is true
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: NVIDIA and Megaspeed are reported to dispute it; no primary corroboration located.

claims.assertion: SPF and Singapore Customs opened an independent investigation in February 2025 into several companies, including Megaspeed International Pte Ltd, and their key officers, for suspected domestic offences concerning potential false declarations in the purchase of servers. The servers had been exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market. SPF was investigating whether they were later routed from Malaysia to another destination, contrary to declarations made in Singapore.
claims.supporting_passage: "The physical servers had been purchased by companies (which were under investigation) and exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market."
excluded_implications: That the servers reached China or any destination beyond Malaysia
That the servers contained NVIDIA products (the statement does not say)
That any offence was committed
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Transit through Singapore with a documented next hop (Malaysia) is established; the final destination is the open question of the investigation.

claims.assertion: On 24 June 2025 the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security carried out a voluntary Post-Shipment Verification check at Megaspeed. MHA states this was the first time Singapore learned of U.S. interest in Megaspeed.
claims.supporting_passage: "On 24 June 2025, the US Bureau of Industry and Security (\"BIS\") conducted a voluntary Post-Shipment Verification (\"PSV\") check at Megaspeed"
claims.scope: U.S. export-control end-use check in Singapore, June 2025
excluded_implications: That the check found a violation
That NVIDIA was involved
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: A PSV check is a routine end-use verification tool; its outcome is not stated.

claims.assertion: In February 2026 SPF, in consultation with the Attorney-General's Chambers, concluded there was insufficient evidence that Megaspeed's then-CEO had committed offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations under investigation. Investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals remain ongoing.
claims.supporting_passage: "SPF's investigations into Megaspeed and six other individuals are ongoing."
claims.scope: Singapore investigation status as of 12 Nov 2026
excluded_implications: Any finding about Megaspeed itself
Any finding about U.S. export-control compliance (outside Singapore's remit)
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: An ongoing investigation is not a charge; an insufficient-evidence conclusion about one officer is not an exoneration of the company.

claims.assertion: Singapore states that the U.S.-based server supplier Supermicro gave limited cooperation, and that since September 2025 Singapore has repeatedly asked DOJ and FBI for assistance and received limited information.
claims.supporting_passage: "Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company."
excluded_implications: That the supplier acted unlawfully
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: This is one government's account of the cooperation; no U.S. response was examined.

claims.assertion: Between February 2025 and July 2026 Singapore charged four individuals and four companies with offences including fraud by false representation in relation to the purchase of servers.
claims.supporting_passage: "Singapore has charged four individuals and four companies in Court between February 2025 and July 2026"
excluded_implications: That these charges concern Megaspeed (the statement does not link them)
That any conviction has occurred
That the servers contained NVIDIA products
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: Charges are allegations under Singapore law until adjudicated.

claims.assertion: MITI states that it has never cleared Megaspeed International or its Malaysian affiliate Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, and that verification visits are routine monitoring, not clearance. Speedmatrix is a data-centre tenant that brings its own servers and AI chips into Malaysia, and bringing AI chips into Malaysia does not currently require a permit. Since July 2025, exporting, re-exporting, transshipping or transiting high-performance U.S. AI chips requires a MITI permit. MITI is working with Royal Malaysian Customs to determine whether any chips have since been re-exported and whether lawfully, and it is working with Singapore and U.S. authorities.
claims.supporting_passage: "it has never cleared Singapore based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd or its Malaysian affiliate, Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd"; "Bringing AI chips into Malaysia does not currently require a permit or a licence."
excluded_implications: That any chips were re-exported
That compute was rented to users in China (the statement is silent on remote access)
That Speedmatrix or Megaspeed broke Malaysian law
That 'not cleared' means 'found non-compliant'
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: 'Never cleared' denies a clearance; it is not an adverse finding.

claims.assertion: On 3 March 2025 Singapore's Home Affairs Minister said servers supplied by Dell and Supermicro to Singapore-based companies went to Malaysia. Whether Malaysia was the final destination was not known. Singapore assessed only that the servers 'may contain Nvidia chips' and described the case as an independent investigation 'unrelated' to U.S. export-control circumvention.
claims.pinpoint: MHA transcript 3 Mar 2025, Minister's opening remarks and answers to questions
claims.supporting_passage: "We assessed that the servers may contain Nvidia chips. I think that's the highest I can put it at, at this point."
claims.scope: Singapore, 3 March 2025 (a pre-cutoff document located post hoc)
excluded_implications: That NVIDIA chips were confirmed
That any chips reached China
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: The Minister declined to speculate on onward movement.

claims.assertion: The short report reportedly alleges that over 20% of NVIDIA's FY2026 compute revenue remained China-driven. Its reported derivation combines third-party market-share estimates with NVIDIA's H20 revenue and per-unit price assumptions. It reportedly alleges that Megaspeed's assets rose from $33m to $3.0bn in 2024, driven by $2.9bn of 'refundable deposits'; that Speedmatrix pledged its business to Apex Enterprise Solutions, whose parent per Singapore filings is Alibaba; and that Aivres (formerly Inspur Systems) supplied over $4bn of servers to Megaspeed/Speedmatrix that NVIDIA would report as U.S. sales. The author disclosed a short position.
claims.pinpoint: Search-index excerpts and secondary summaries; page numbers unavailable
claims.scope: Allegations by a disclosed short seller, 13 May 2026
excluded_implications: That any allegation is true
That a financing relationship implies control of end use
That chips reached China
claims.counterevidence_or_alternative: No allegation was traced to a primary document examined in this pass. The registry and trade data it cites were not accessed.

errata.original_text: The Singapore Police Force stated on 30 October 2026 that 'Investigations into Megaspeed are ongoing', that Singapore does not implement foreign unilateral export controls but acts against fraud, and that no investigation was conducted in respect of the individual named in the WSJ article.
errata.correction: The original paraphrase dropped the qualifier 'such' and could be read as saying no investigation of the named individual took place. SI1-PST-013 (paras 3, 7–8) shows she was investigated for suspected domestic offences. The assertion now quotes the qualifier.
errata.reason: The original wording overstated what the SPF statement denied.

errata.original_text: F6 ... Immediate reaction to the report was positive (CAR[0,+1] +4.6% vs SMH, t = 2.2)
errata.correction: Eight post-event tests were run (4 windows × 2 benchmarks); the Bonferroni-adjusted two-sided 5% threshold is |t| > 2.73. CAR[0,+1] vs SMH (t = 2.22) is nominally significant only. The direction (positive) stands.
errata.reason: The first pass never relied on significance for attribution; the statistical weight of the result is reduced.
